summary: Verified the 5:30 IST timezone drift fix end-to-end. Backend: 5/5 pytest cases pass — /api/vendor/all-outlets-orders returns created_at/ready_at/collected_at as tz-aware '+00:00' ISO; /api/vendor/reports/sales-orders paginated rows tz-aware; CSV export header is 'Date & Time (UTC)' and rows are tz-aware ISO. Cross-panel match confirmed at API level (same order same instant across /api/orders and /api/vendor/all-outlets-orders, drift < 2s). Frontend: with browser context forced to Asia/Kolkata (to simulate real IST user), all 5 sampled cards on /vendor/all-orders show IST times exactly matching UTC+5:30 conversion of the backend value (drift = 0 minutes). Same order CRV-AUDA01 renders identical time '07:12:07 pm' on both /vendor/all-orders and /vendor/orders — no 5:30 drift. Collected/Ready badges render with correct testids. Outlet chips, counts, auto-refresh footer, top-bar outlet switch and per-outlet counter all still work.
critical_code_review_comments: vendor_reports.py _iso_utc helper mirrors orders.py normalisation cleanly — good. Consider extracting into a shared util (e.g. app/backend/utils/datetime_utils.py) so future routers can't reintroduce this class of bug.

AllOrders.js uses `toLocaleString('en-IN', {...})` without an explicit timeZone: 'Asia/Kolkata'. That means the display follows the *user's device* timezone, not necessarily IST. If a user in a different timezone (or a mis-set device clock) views the page they'll see their local time, not IST. If IST is contractually required, pass `timeZone: 'Asia/Kolkata'`. Not a regression — matches Vendor/Employee Orders pages — but worth flagging.

Backend regression tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_tz_iso.py.
rca_of_the_issue: Bug: /api/vendor/all-outlets-orders and vendor sales report endpoints returned Motor-fetched naive datetimes as ISO strings without a tz suffix. Browsers parse a tz-less ISO ('2026-09-09T13:42:07.888') as *local* time (IST), which then rendered as the actual UTC value 5:30 too early. Reference correct impl in /api/orders normalises via .replace(tzinfo=utc).astimezone(utc).isoformat(). Fix: added _iso_utc() helper in vendor_reports.py and applied to created_at (+ new ready_at/collected_at) in all_outlets_orders, and to created_at in paginated sales-orders + CSV export. Verified: backend now emits '+00:00' suffix; IST-configured browser renders correct local time; cross-panel drift eliminated.
